candidates.title: Wireless Power Transfer in Space using Flexible, Lightweight, Coherent Arrays
candidates.notes: 2024 paper on space WPT; rectenna efficiency 40% for their demo setup, up to 70% under optimum conditions (X-band). CubeSat-scale demonstration, not MW-scale, but provides engineering-grounded rectenna efficiency figures and discusses atmospheric transmission. Accessible via arxiv HTML.

candidates.title: A Lightweight Space-based Solar Power Generation and Transmission Satellite
candidates.notes: Contains 7-14% end-to-end efficiency figure (includes solar panel collection, not just beaming chain). Abstract only accessible; full paper behind arxiv PDF.

entries.notes: Best accessible source is a CubeSat-scale WPT demonstration paper (not MW-scale as recommended). OSTI SPS technical reports are binary PDFs not accessible via WebFetch. The gap calls specifically for MW-scale SPS data (JAXA, DoE); the extracted paper provides sub-gap rectenna efficiency figures (40-70%) but lacks atmospheric loss modeling and MW-scale demonstration data. A dedicated OSTI extraction via the add-source pipeline on a JAXA or DOE SPS report with a direct HTML landing page would better fill this gap.

candidates.title: The Helium-3 Shortage: Supply, Demand, and Options for Congress (CRS Report R41419)
candidates.notes: Comprehensive CRS report covering: US production ~8,000 L/year from weapons program; Russian imports ~25,000 L/year 2004-2008 (now suspended); DOE reserve fell from 235,000 L (2001) to 50,000 L (2010); historical auction price $40-85/L; post-shortage commercial price up to $2,000/L; unsubsidized production cost $11,000-18,000/L. Highly accessible HTML version.

candidates.title: Supply and Demand of Helium-3 (NIDC)
candidates.notes: NIDC policy page. Demand peaked at 70,000 L/year (2008); current federal demand under 6,000 L/year. Overview only — no production rates, prices, or supply breakdown. Not extracted (CRS report is more comprehensive).

candidates.title: Managing Critical Isotopes: Weaknesses in DOE's Management of Helium-3 (GAO)
candidates.notes: GAO report on He3 management. Did not triage due to budget; likely corroborates CRS data. CRS report already extracted.

candidates.title: Congressional Hearing: Causes and Consequences of the Helium-3 Supply Crisis
candidates.notes: Congressional hearing HTML — would contain testimony from DOE officials with production data. Not attempted due to budget; CRS report covers same timeframe.

candidates.title: The Helium-3 Shortage: Supply, Demand, and Options for Congress (PDF)
candidates.notes: PDF version of same CRS report — extracted HTML version instead.

entries.notes: CRS R41419 comprehensively covers the He3 supply/demand/price gap. Key data: US production ~8,000 L/year; historical price $40-85/L rising to $2,000/L commercial; unsubsidized production cost $11,000-18,000/L (~$63-103M/kg, far above the $28-34M/kg estimate in the analysis — the analysis estimate may be based on allocated/subsidized prices). The report also quantifies the DOE reserve drawdown (235k→50k liters 2001-2010) and the Russian export suspension. This source substantially fills gap G-15.
